rationale: Greek loanword δόκιμος 'approved, tested, proven'. Used here as the technical title applied to the catechumen who has been tested in the aeons of Light. Lyc. ⲁ for ⲇ (regular Lyc. orthographic feature). The kephalaion explains the title via its connection to ⲇⲟⲕⲓⲙⲁⲍⲉ 'test, prove'.
Greek loanword δοκιμάζειν 'to test, examine, prove'. Lyc. ⲁ for ⲇ. The verb underlying the title ⲁⲟⲕⲓⲙⲟⲥ — those who are 'proven' have been δοκιμάζωd in the aeons of Light.

Demonstrative ⲡⲓ- + ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ 'the four' (Lyc. collective form of ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ, in glossary). Reference uncertain in this context — possibly the four cosmic ages, four ranks, or four classes. Since the glossary already has ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ for 'the four', this entry documents the demonstrative variant ⲡⲓϩⲧⲁⲩ.
Standard Coptic ⲣⲉⲛ/ⲣⲁⲛ 'name' with article. With demonstrative ⲡⲓⲣⲉⲛ = 'this name'. Cf. accumulated ϯⲡⲉⲛ 'to give a name' (Lyc. ⲡⲉⲛ for ⲣⲉⲛ); here the ⲣⲉⲛ form attests the standard spelling.

Standard Coptic noun for 'number, reckoning' from ⲱⲡ 'count' (cf. accumulated ⲱⲡ 'to count/reckon' and ⲡⲉϩⲟⲩⲏⲥ 'rooted'). Paired with ϣⲓ 'measure' as the standard 'measure-and-number' doublet for divine reckoning.

Lyc. qualitative form, possibly reflex of ⲏⲡ 'be counted, belong' (cf. accumulated ⲏⲡ ⲁ-) with vowel-form ⲏⲓⲧ. 'The aeons that belong to the Light' = those reckoned/numbered as Light's domain. Confidence moderate; alternative reading 'established/firm' from a different stative also possible.

Unusual form with double ⲡ. Most plausibly a scribal variant or copying error for ⲡⲟⲣⲟ 'kingship' (Lyc. for ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ, in glossary). Construction ⲁϥϯ ⲡⲟⲣⲡⲟ ⲛⲉⲩ matches the well-attested idiom ⲁϥϯ ⲡⲟⲣⲟ ⲛⲉⲩ 'he gave kingship to them'. Documenting this variant for parallel-search purposes.
